title: RBI in Geelong: Corio Bay Refinery and Fuel Storage
description: Remote risk-based inspection for the Geelong refinery and its fuel storage on Corio Bay: damage mechanisms, Victorian OHS and MHF rules, and inspection plans.
h1: Risk-based inspection for Geelong and the Corio Bay refinery
intro: Geelong holds one of Australia's two remaining crude oil refineries, Viva Energy's plant at Corio on the shore of Corio Bay, which is generally reported to make around half of the fuel used in Victoria. This page is for the inspection and integrity people who plan its equipment and the fuel storage that goes with it. It covers the damage mechanisms that residue cracking, crude processing and a bayside site add, how Victoria's own occupational health and safety rules frame a risk-based programme, and how Atlantis runs the study remotely while your inspectors carry out the field checks.

highlights.h: Victoria's rules, not the model laws
highlights.p: Victoria kept its own OHS Act and 2017 regulations rather than adopting the national model. Plant registration, the major hazard facility licence and dangerous goods storage all sit in Victorian instruments, and the RBI method statement refers to them by name.

highlights.h: Out-of-service plant stays in the register
highlights.p: Units isolated for a long period do not stop deteriorating. The register keeps them, records how they are preserved and sets what must be inspected before they return, so a restart is planned from evidence rather than from the last report written before shutdown.

highlights.h: Bay air and cool, wet winters
highlights.p: Salt carried off Corio Bay, long damp winters and the temperature swings of hot northerly days all reach insulated lines and tank shells. CUI and external corrosion are ranked on exposure and insulation condition, not on design temperature alone.

sections.h: The refinery at Corio and what it supplies
p: Shell opened the Geelong refinery in 1954 and sold it in 2014 to Viva Energy, which owns and operates it today. It processes crude delivered by sea into petrol, diesel and jet fuel for the Victorian market. The federal Fuel Security Services Payment, extended in March 2026 to 30 June 2030, supports Geelong and Lytton through periods of weak refining margins, and refiners taking part have committed to keep operating until at least mid-2027.

In April 2026 a fire in the refinery's alkylation unit cut output for several weeks. Viva Energy said in June 2026 that the residue catalytic cracking unit and associated units were returning to service, that production was expected to recover to more than 90 per cent of normal capacity, and that the refinery would run without the alkylation unit throughout 2027 while repair or replacement options were assessed. For inspection planning that means an operating refinery with one major unit isolated, which the next section deals with.

Alongside the process units sit the refinery's crude and product tankage, the transfer lines between them and the marine berth that serves the site. The study treats tanks, lines and process units as one register with separate corrosion loops, because one owner answers for all of them inside the same safety management system.

sections.h: Equipment that is isolated, preserved or waiting to restart
p: An RBI model is usually written for equipment that is running. Units that stand isolated for months, whether after damage, during a long repair or because the market for their product has changed, need a different treatment. Process-side corrosion stops, but wet air, condensate, residual hydrocarbon, sludge and chlorides left in the system can attack internals that were protected while hot and flowing. Austenitic stainless steel carrying sulfide scale can suffer polythionic acid stress corrosion cracking once moisture and air reach it, unless it is neutralised or kept dry.

The register therefore records each isolated item's preservation method, such as nitrogen blanketing, dry air, chemical neutralisation or simple draining, and the date it was last confirmed. Probability is assessed for the idle period itself, and the plan carries a pre-restart list: which items need internal examination, which need thickness checks where condensate collects, which relief devices and instruments need recertification, and which can return on external inspection alone. Repaired or replacement equipment enters the register with its design data and a baseline inspection rather than inheriting the old history.

Equipment around an isolated unit matters as much as the unit. Lines that once carried flow and now sit as dead legs behind closed valves, and shared relief or flare headers that see different service, are added to the review, because their damage mechanisms change the moment the unit stops.

sections.h: Where risk usually concentrates in the process units
p: A refinery with residue cracking runs a long list of damage mechanisms, and the study ranks them unit by unit. The table shows the pattern the corrosion loop review usually follows at a site of this kind; the actual loops are drawn from your P&IDs, heat and material balances and operating data, and assigned to API 571 in workshops with your own specialists.

sections.h: Corio Bay air, winter rain and hot northerly days
p: Geelong's climate is temperate rather than tropical, which tempts some programmes to rank external corrosion low. The site argues otherwise. Salt carried off the bay settles on cooler surfaces and is concentrated by repeated wetting and drying; winter brings frequent rain and long damp spells; and summer northerlies can lift temperatures sharply for a day or two before a cool change, cycling insulated equipment through condensation.

The CUI assessment follows API RP 583 and ranks each insulated item on its real operating temperature profile, insulation and jacketing type, the sealing at supports and penetrations, and its exposure to bay winds, deluge testing or cooling tower drift. Equipment that normally runs hot but spends weeks cold during an outage, as an isolated unit does, moves up the list. Austenitic stainless lines under wet insulation are assessed for external chloride stress corrosion cracking rather than for thinning.

Tank shells and roofs, pipe racks near the waterline and loading line supports are ranked for atmospheric corrosion on the same evidence. Coating condition surveys are credited for what they reveal about the steel beneath; a survey that records appearance only, without film thickness or adhesion, earns less credit than one that measures.

sections.h: Victoria's OHS framework and the refinery's licence
p: Victoria regulates workplaces under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017, administered by WorkSafe Victoria, rather than under the national model laws most other states and territories use. The 2017 regulations carry Victoria's own plant registration requirements, and Part 5.2 sets up the major hazard facility regime: an operator notifies WorkSafe once holdings pass 10 per cent of a Schedule 14 threshold quantity, the facility is registered while it prepares its safety case, and WorkSafe then grants a licence that can run for up to five years.

General requirements for storing and handling dangerous goods come from the Dangerous Goods (Storage and Handling) Regulations 2022, with AS 1940 as the technical benchmark for flammable and combustible liquids. Pressure equipment in service is inspected to AS/NZS 3788, now in its 2024 edition, which in refinery practice often runs alongside API 510, API 570 and API 653.

For RBI this means three documents have to agree: the safety case, which describes the major incidents and the controls relied on; the inspection procedure, which sets how intervals are decided under AS/NZS 3788; and the RBI register, which records the basis for each date. The study cross-checks its consequence cases against the safety case and writes the method statement so the refinery can adopt it into the procedure ahead of its next licence assessment.

sections.h: Planning horizons: shutdowns, licences and fuel security
p: Inspection plans at Geelong work to three clocks at once. The turnaround cycle sets when major units can be opened. The major hazard facility licence, renewed on a cycle of up to five years, sets when the regulator next examines the safety case and the evidence behind it. And the fuel security arrangements, now extended to mid-2030, frame how far ahead the owner is planning capital and maintenance.

An RBI plan helps by stating, for every item, whether its next inspection is on-stream or needs a shutdown, and what the risk would become if it slipped to the following window. Items whose risk would cross the owner's target before the next planned shutdown are flagged early, so the planning team can choose between an on-stream technique, a short unit outage or an interim operating limit. Where an item's assessed date falls beyond the planning horizon, the plan still sets a review date, so a long interval never becomes an unexamined one.

sections.h: Running the study on Melbourne time
p: Geelong keeps Australian Eastern Standard Time, ten hours ahead of UTC, and moves to daylight time from the first Sunday in October to the first Sunday in April. Hyderabad is four and a half hours behind in the Australian winter and five and a half in summer, so workshops booked for a Geelong afternoon land in the Hyderabad morning. Houston sits fifteen to seventeen hours behind, depending on both countries' daylight saving, which suits short calls at the start of the Geelong day.

Before the first workshop the data room receives P&IDs and PFDs, heat and material balances, datasheets and manufacturer's data reports, Victorian registration records, inspection and thickness history, preservation records for isolated equipment, historian extracts for temperatures and process chemistry, and the integrity operating windows in force. A data-gap log follows, so the site can decide which gaps to close before the risk calculation and which to leave to conservative assumptions.

Corrosion loops and damage mechanisms are then reviewed with your process, operations, corrosion and inspection specialists by video. Risk is calculated at the level the scope calls for, from a qualitative screen to a quantitative API RP 581 assessment or your corporate RBI standard, and each item receives a plan with method, coverage, expected effectiveness and due date. No travel to Geelong is needed for the study; the field checks it calls for, from insulation condition to extra thickness readings, are carried out by your own inspectors or your existing inspection contractor.

sections.h: Who accepts the plan, and what follows a finding
p: Each interval is a recommendation with its basis written down. Acceptance belongs to the competent person the refinery's inspection procedure names, often its own inspection engineer, while the regulator and the insurer review the programme as a whole. Atlantis does not act as inspector of record and is not a registered inspection body in Victoria.

When inspection finds damage that needs an assessment of continued operation, that assessment stays with the owner's engineer. Once it is made, the result goes back into the register, the related items in the same corrosion loop are reassessed and their next due dates move with the new evidence.

faqs.q: Can the study include units that are isolated for a long period?
faqs.a: Yes. Isolated equipment stays in the register with its preservation method and the date that method was last confirmed, and it is assessed for the damage that can happen while it stands idle. The plan sets a pre-restart inspection list for each item, and any repaired or replaced equipment enters the register with design data and a baseline inspection rather than the old history.

faqs.q: Does WorkSafe Victoria approve RBI intervals?
faqs.a: WorkSafe does not approve individual inspection dates. It licenses a major hazard facility on the strength of its safety case and assesses whether the operator's controls, mechanical integrity among them, are adequate. The owner's procedure names the competent person who accepts intervals, and a study that ties each interval to the safety case's release scenarios makes that assessment easier to support.

faqs.q: Which standard should the RBI method statement refer to in Victoria?
faqs.a: Usually AS/NZS 3788:2024 for the in-service inspection obligations, with API RP 580 and API RP 581 or ASME PCC-3 for the risk method, and API 510, 570 and 653 where the site inspects to them. Procedures written against the 2006 edition of the Australian Standard should be restated against the current one, which is also a good moment to review the RBI method.

faqs.q: How does the study treat CUI at a temperate site like Geelong?
faqs.a: It ranks CUI on exposure and operating history rather than climate averages: salt from the bay, winter rain, deluge testing, insulation and jacketing type, sealing at penetrations and how often equipment passes through the corrosive temperature range. Equipment that runs hot but stands cold during outages moves up the ranking, and screening techniques are credited only for what they can find.

faqs.q: Are the refinery's tanks covered by the same study?
faqs.a: They can be. Tanks, transfer lines and loading lines are assessed in the same register as the process units but with their own corrosion loops. Out-of-service dates use API 653's RBI-based internal interval, validated and reviewed at least every ten years, and floor scan coverage and cathodic protection history are the inputs that most often limit the credit a tank receives.

faqs.q: Does anyone need to travel to Geelong for the study?
faqs.a: No. The study runs remotely from your documents, historian data and video workshops, and it needs no travel. Walkdowns, preservation checks on isolated equipment and any thickness readings the data-gap log asks for are done by your own inspectors or your inspection contractor, working from a verification list that states the location, method and coverage of each check.

faqs.q: How do workshops fit around Victorian working hours?
faqs.a: Workshops are booked in Geelong's afternoon, which falls in the Hyderabad morning, and kept short so shift staff can attend. During daylight saving the gap with Hyderabad widens by an hour and the schedule moves with it. Analysis and drafting continue between sessions, so actions raised in one workshop are ready for the next.

The competent person named in the refinery's inspection procedure. The study proposes each interval with its reasoning and the code limits it respects, but it does not approve intervals, and Atlantis is not the inspector of record for any item. Decisions on continued operation after damage is found stay with the owner's engineer.
